control_action: create or normalize a workflow draft
observed_behavior: normalizeWorkflow independently invents per-node binding IDs, omits ports for partially supplied nodes, leaves effect grants empty, and supplies no default executor adapter, so normalized drafts can fail their own validator.
expected_behavior: Missing workflow fields receive one internally consistent bounded grant, binding, adapter, and typed port baseline; explicitly supplied invalid values remain visible and fail closed.
operational_impact: Workflow Builder initialization and node creation can yield a non-runnable candidate before intentional edits, obscuring real user errors with editor-generated contract failures.

discovery_evidence.claim: The normalized typed workflow validity assertion failed.
Node, grant, binding, and adapter defaults are derived independently and do not form one valid contract.

next_action: Derive one shared default grant/binding identity before node normalization, add ports only when omitted, and synthesize the identity adapter only when adapters are omitted.

open_load.detail: Draft opens but may start invalid.

user_edit_action.detail: Users can edit generated contracts but must repair editor-created mismatches.

input_validation.detail: Validator correctly detects undeclared bindings, grants, adapters, and ports.

authorization.detail: Generated declarations are draft-only, but their identities are inconsistent.

result_acknowledgement.detail: Errors are shown but normalization created them.

failure_handling.detail: Save fails closed; no coherent default recovery exists.

recovery_rollback.detail: Manual repair is possible but unnecessary work.
